nodes.notes: Promoted 2026-10-30 from brainstorm agentic-performance (13 accepted of 70). Research triage: docs/design-notes/agent-performance-research-triage.md. Acceptance and touch zones still to author per leaf; M10.13 defaults to logs untracked.
nodes.title: Agent loop performance and observability

acceptance: The event schema gains the types launched and first_output; the wrapper appends launched (detail: argv[0], harness, resumed flag) right after the harness process starts and first_output on the first stdout line it reads; both carry the existing at timestamp and nothing else new
worker sync --ack records, per worker, the time the ack happened and the highest seq acked, in the existing sync state file, without changing what sync returns

specy-road worker timeline <worker id or NODE_ID> prints one line per phase with its duration: delegated to launched, launched to first output, first output to the turn's end (turn_completed, completion or error), and end to acked, each marked unknown when an event is missing; --json prints the same as an object; the rendering lives in worker_cli_render.py so worker_cli.py stays under the 400-line cap
docs/orchestration-workers.md lists the two new events in its event list and documents worker timeline in the command table; tests cover A1 to A3
nodes.goal: If we do this, active wall-clock per leaf by phase moves from unmeasured to measured, which is the precondition for every other idea here being checked
nodes.title: Record phase timestamps in the event log and print a per-leaf timeline

acceptance: The event schema gains the type usage with the nullable detail fields input_tokens, cached_input_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_tokens, cost_usd, cost_is_estimate, num_turns and harness_version; a field the harness did not report is null, never 0

The wrapper appends one usage event per turn end: the Claude Code adapter fills it from the result line (its cumulative cost converted to a delta against the previous turn on resume, cost_is_estimate true), the Codex adapter from turn.completed.usage, and the Cursor adapter from whatever its result line carries, else nulls
worker usage <worker id or NODE_ID> prints tokens and cost per attempt with model and harness and a total per node; --json prints the same; rendering lives in worker_cli_render.py
docs/orchestration-workers.md lists the usage event and the command; tests cover A1 to A3 with recorded sample lines per harness
nodes.goal: If we do this, cost per role becomes comparable across harnesses because every adapter writes the same shape
nodes.title: Normalised usage event in the worker log

acceptance: Every append_event also updates the modification time of one file, work/.workers/FLAG

worker sync --wait [--timeout SECONDS] (default 600) returns as soon as FLAG changes after the call started or an unacked event already exists, then prints the usual sync output; on timeout it prints the empty delta and exits 2; it checks the file every 250 ms and uses no OS watch API
The wait runs in the calling process only: no child process survives the command, and an interrupt exits cleanly without a traceback

docs/orchestration-workers.md documents --wait in the loop section and command table and docs/grind-session.md mentions it for step mode; tests cover A1 and A2 using a thread that appends an event during the wait
nodes.goal: If we do this, coordination latency between an event being written and the coordinator observing it moves from one coordinator turn to sub-second because the coordinator stops guessing when to look
nodes.title: Replace per-worker polling with a single mailbox flag file and a foreground --wait

acceptance: A model profile's access block accepts launch_mode with the values full or bare (absent means full); model_profiles rejects any other value with a message naming the profile, and specy-road models show prints it
The Claude Code adapter passes --bare on launch and on resume when the profile says bare and never passes it when the profile says full; a custom channels.cli is left as written

The started event the adapter parses from the system/init line carries detail with the harness version when the line has one, the tool names, the MCP server names and the plugin names reported, and inferred_mode set to bare when the tool list is only the bare-mode set, else full
When inferred_mode differs from the profile's launch_mode, the adapter also yields an error event naming both modes, so worker sync shows it on the next turn

docs/orchestration-models.md documents launch_mode, the vendor's bare-by-default note with its URL and the date read, and the API-key consequence of bare; the model-profiles README schema lists the field; the two shipped Claude profiles set launch_mode: full; tests cover A1 to A4
nodes.goal: If we do this, a vendor default change cannot silently strip workers of their harness tools
nodes.title: Pin harness discovery mode per profile

acceptance: A profile's access block accepts effort_by_role mapping coordinator, executor and reviewer to a key of effort_map; model_profiles rejects an unknown role or a level not in effort_map, naming the profile, and models show prints the mapping

A roster channels.cli may name {effort}; prompt --channel cli and worker delegate replace it with the harness's token for the role's level (Claude Code: --effort <level>; Codex: -c model_reasoning_effort=<level>; Cursor: empty) and, when the profile sets a role effort but the command names no {effort}, print one note that the command takes no effort

The default Claude Code and Codex launch and resume commands built by worker_adapters carry the executor's effort flag when the profile sets one; the child environment of every worker has CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL unset, so the profile wins

docs/orchestration-models.md documents effort_by_role and {effort}; the model-profiles README lists the field; the shipped Claude profiles set executor and reviewer to the model's documented default level and coordinator one level below, with a comment pointing at M10.6; tests cover A1 to A3
nodes.goal: If we do this, reviewer and coordinator turns get cheaper and faster without touching executor quality
nodes.title: Per-role effort in model profiles

acceptance: scripts/review_effort_study.py replays recorded review packets through a roster reviewer at two effort levels and writes one CSV row per packet, level and model with the verdict and block reasons; it calls only the roster's channels.cli, never a model API

docs/design-notes/reviewer-effort-study.md records the protocol, the packets used (node ids and commits), the results table, and a decision per model family using the rule that a default is lowered only when verdicts agree on every packet and block reasons overlap
The shipped Claude profiles' effort_by_role values are confirmed or changed with a comment citing the note
nodes.goal: If we do this, the per-role effort defaults rest on a measurement instead of the seed article's general claim
nodes.title: Measure whether lower reviewer effort changes verdicts

acceptance: review-packet inlines at most --max-diff-lines lines of diff (default 1500); past the cap the packet keeps the first files whole, lists every remaining changed path with its added and removed line counts, and names the full diff it wrote to work/reviews/<NODE_ID>/DIFF.patch; --max-diff-lines 0 means no cap and no DIFF.patch; a packet under the cap is byte-identical to today's
brief writes one header line with the brief's total size in bytes and its three largest sections by size, and prints a warning on stderr naming them when the total exceeds 65536 bytes
grind-session --plan --json --fields <comma list> prints only those top-level keys; an unknown key is an error naming the valid keys
validate prints the no-acceptance warnings as one line per class, counting the leaves and listing their ids, instead of one line per leaf; the per-leaf fix hint appears once
docs/dev-workflow.md documents the diff cap, DIFF.patch and the brief size line; docs/grind-session.md documents --fields; tests cover A1 to A4
nodes.goal: If we do this, uncached input per turn shrinks because dumps become summaries with a pointer
nodes.title: Output budgets with --full on packets, briefs and plans

acceptance: review record accepts --launch-mode full|bare|explicit and stores it on the review record; the schema allows the field and handoff status prints it per review

prompt --role reviewer for a Claude Code roster entry without channels.cli builds the command with --bare, --add-dir for the reviews directory and no repository hooks or MCP servers, and prints that bare mode needs an API key
The reviewer prompt tells the reviewer to pass --launch-mode with the mode it ran under; sr/tools/claude-review.sh in this repository runs with --bare
docs/orchestration-review.md documents the field and why a fresh-session reviewer runs without repository hooks; tests cover A1 and A2
nodes.goal: If we do this, reviewer start-up is faster and a hostile branch cannot run code in the reviewer's session
nodes.title: Reviewers launch without repo hooks or MCP

acceptance: The worker record gains last_output_at, which the wrapper updates from stdout lines at most once every five seconds

worker sync and worker list mark a running worker stalled when last_output_at is older than policy.stall_after_seconds (default 600) and append one stalled event (new type) naming the seconds silent and the last summary; the next output line clears the mark and a later silence may raise it again
Both schemas accept the new field and type; orchestration_config exposes the policy key with its default
docs/orchestration-workers.md adds stalled to the flags table and the event list; docs/orchestration.md adds the policy key to its policy table; tests cover A1 and A2 with a fake clock
nodes.goal: If we do this, active wall-clock per leaf moves because dead time inside a stalled worker is surfaced at the next sync instead of at the end of the night
nodes.title: Emit a stalled event when a worker goes silent past a threshold

acceptance: docs/philosophy-and-scope.md gains a section titled Where specy-road sits that says other tools now drive coding-agent CLIs as workers, names Microsoft Agent Framework, LiteLLM's harness feature and Bernstein each with a primary URL and the date read, and states the four commitments that together are specy-road's: the roadmap graph in the repo, separated roles with fresh-session distinct-family reviewers, reviews bound to a commit, and tracked files plus shell commands as the only surface
README.md's Why teams use it list gains one bullet with that positioning, linking the new section; the What it is paragraph is otherwise unchanged
docs/orchestration.md's opening paragraph gains one sentence pointing at the new section
Every statement about another tool is one its own documentation makes; nothing from the secondary-source list in docs/design-notes/agent-performance-research-triage.md section 5 is repeated as fact
nodes.goal: If we do this, adopters evaluate specy-road on the right axis and fewer feature requests ask for a generic agent runner
nodes.title: Position the docs on governance, not on CLI workers

acceptance: The executor prompt written at pickup gains one paragraph telling the agent to use its harness's own subagents for independent verification and search inside the leaf (running the named test files in parallel, searching the tree) and never for edits outside the touch zones, and that a subagent's report is data
prompt --role executor includes the same paragraph only when the model profile's access.subagents starts with yes

docs/orchestration-models.md gains a short subsection on parallel work inside a leaf under Choosing and prompting models, and the model-profiles README states which access.subagents values enable it; tests cover A1 and A2
nodes.goal: If we do this, executor wall-clock falls on test-heavy leaves because the harness already parallelises
nodes.title: Document the harness-subagent recipe for parallel work inside a leaf

acceptance: The GUI serves GET /api/workers (one row per worker: id, node, harness, model, state, last event, total cost) and GET /api/workers/{id}/events (the event log with the phase durations and usage totals), read from the main worktree's work/.workers and never written

A Workers drawer in the PM Gantt UI lists workers per leaf; selecting one shows a phase bar built from the timeline durations, the event list with tool-call lines, cost per attempt, and stall markers when stalled events exist
No new npm dependency; npm run lint, npm test and npm run build pass from gui/pm-gantt
docs/pm-gui.md documents the drawer; Python tests cover both routes and one vitest covers the phase-bar math
nodes.goal: If we do this, maintainers find slow or wrong leaf runs in minutes because the log is browsable instead of read as JSONL
nodes.title: Visual explorer for worker event logs in the PM GUI

acceptance: roadmap/git-workflow.yaml accepts track_worker_logs with the values off, events or full (absent means off); validate rejects any other value

With events, the wrapper mirrors each worker's event log to work/worker-logs/<NODE_ID>/<worker id>.events.jsonl (a tracked path) and finish-this-task commits that directory with the leaf; with full the raw output log is mirrored too; with off nothing is written outside work/.workers
The ignore rules the toolkit writes keep work/.workers/ and work/.worktrees/ ignored in every mode and never ignore work/worker-logs/
docs/git-workflow.md documents the key with the default and the size warning; docs/orchestration-workers.md and the work README say where logs live in each mode; tests cover A1 to A3
nodes.goal: If we do this, teams that want an audit trail get one without a side system, and teams that do not keep their repo clean
nodes.title: A project setting decides whether agent logs are tracked in git
